newsitem.title: USA: Westchester Cty, N.Y. weighs courthouse renovation.
newsitem.headline: Westchester Cty, N.Y. weighs courthouse renovation.

text.p: Westchester County, N.Y., has outgrown its courthouse, opened in 1974, and is trying to decide whether to spend $65 million to renovate the building, according to county officials.
The courthouse facade has started to chip away, officials noted.
Other options that are being evaluated include leasing a new or existing building in White Plains, the county seat.
But triple-A rated Westchester County has just about ruled out building another new courthouse because that approach would be too costly.

The decision to refurbish or seek a new court house also is being driven by state regulations, approved nearly five years ago, that the courthouse is not in compliance with, explained Ralph Butler, first deputy commissioner of public works.
Butler, who speculated that it might cost the county as much as $130 million to build a new courthouse, said the expense of the various options likely will decide which is chosen.
"We're always looking for what is the best way we can go forward at the least expense," he said. "Probably, if the courts had not changed the regulations, we would not have gone forward with this."
The county spent $33.5 million building the current courthouse, which does not have enough room for all its courts.

While the county would have to finance a renovation by issuing $65 million of general obligation bonds, leasing a new building or one that was refurbished to meet its requirements likely would require it to only pay rent.

The final decision will be made by the county's Board of . Acquisition and Contracts, but the board is not expected to finish for months its review of the various proposals that developers recently submitted.
"Right now, the county executive has not set a time frame," Butler said.
